Scientific Evidence: Early toxicology data reviewed by EPA did not indicate carcinogenicity
Legal Decision: EPA first registers glyphosate for use as a herbicide in the United States under FIFRA. Group E classification, no evidence of cancer in humans or required warning labels.
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: Monsanto (original inventor) promoted glyphosate as a safe, broad-spectrum herbicide; agricultural industry embraced the product.

Scientific Evidence: US EPA's own mouse study showed tumor increases, but not in humans
Legal Decision: Group C hazard classification possibly carcinogenic to humans, add warning label
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: Industry challenged interpretation of the animal data; public interest groups began questioning glyphosate safety.

Scientific Evidence: Re-evaluated mouse data; EPA concluded the tumor findings were not predictive of human cancer risk.
Legal Decision: Glyphosate reclassified as Group E; EPA reaffirmed registration in 1993 without cancer warning.
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: Monsanto and agricultural lobbies supported the downgrade; environmental NGOs expressed concern.

Scientific Evidence: Re-affirm previous 1991 statements in a report from the National Academy of Sciences', Pesticides in the Diets of Infants & Children.
Legal Decision: Glyphosate reregistered without a cancer warning on labels.
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: Agribusiness continued lobbying against precautionary measures; glyphosate adoption accelerated with transgenic glyphosate restant crops.

Scientific Evidence: Discussions of to what extent pesticides concentrate within food as evidence for violation of the Delaney clause
Legal Decision: The Food Quality Protection Act (FQPA) is passed, requiring continuous review of existing pesticides. (California ex. rel. Van de Kamp v. Reilly) rule against the EPA for food pesticide contamination.
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: The people of California, AFL-CIO, Natural Resources Defense Council sued the EPA and manufacturers

Scientific Evidence: Early cohort studies in USA, Canada, and Sweden suggest a possible link between glyphosate exposure and non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL).
Legal Decision: No regulatory action; EPA continues to maintain Group E classification.
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: Academic researchers publish findings; environmental NGOs cite early evidence in advocacy campaigns.

Scientific Evidence: Program mandates comprehensive re-evaluation of existing pesticide data on a 15-year cycle.
Legal Decision: Glyphosate entered the registration review pipeline under Statutory basis: FIFRA § 3(g).
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: Industry stakeholders expected the process to be science-based and efficient; NGOs pushed for thoroughness.

Scientific Evidence: EPA begins a comprehensive human health and ecological risk reassessment.
Legal Decision: Work plan for introducing glyphosate; Statutory trigger: FIFRA § 3(g).
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: NRDC files a petition raising science concerns; EPA extends the review timeline to address the petition and subsequent IARC review.
Citation 1: Smith, C. (2019). Glyphosate Proposed Interim Registration Review Decision Case Number 0178. US EPA. https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/2019-04/documents/glyphosate-pid-signed.pdf

Scientific Evidence: EPA issues a Generic Data Call-In (GDCI) for glyphosate, requiring registrants to conduct additional toxicity and ecological studies.
Legal Decision: Data requirements imposed under FIFRA.
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: Glyphosate manufacturers/companies (including Monsanto/Bayer) fund and submit required studies. EPA issues a Generic Data Call-In (GDCI) for glyphosate, requiring registrants to conduct additional toxicity and ecological studies.
Citation 1: US EPA. (2024a, August 27). Glyphosate. EPA. Ingredients Used in Pesticide Products. https://www.epa.gov/ingredients-used-pesticide-products/glyphosate

Scientific Evidence: IARC Working Group (17 independent experts from 11 countries) concluded: limited evidence in humans, sufficient evidence in animals, strong evidence for genotoxicity.
Legal Decision: IARC classification becomes the basis for subsequent US litigation.
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: Monsanto protests the classification as inconsistent with all other regulatory agencies. Environmental groups cite IARC as validation of glyphosate dangers. IARC classification sparks global regulatory re-examinations; EPA and others defend prior conclusions.
Regulatory Outcome Categorical: Scientific event — no direct regulatory change
Citation 1: IARC WHO. (2019). IARC Monograph on Glyphosate. Media Center. https://www.iarc.who.int/featured-news/%20media-centre-iarc-news-glyphosate

Scientific Evidence: Scientific Advisory Panel (SAP) examined epidemiological, animal, and genotoxicity data; panel did not reach consensus on many recommendations.
Legal Decision: SAP advice informs EPA's scientific posture but is not legally binding.
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: Industry and NGOs both submitted comments to SAP; transparency of the process debated. SAP report published March 2017; EPA begins updating its Issue Paper.
Citation 1: US EPA. (2024b, August 27). Ingredients Used  in Pesticide Products. US EPA. https://www.epa.gov/ingredients-used-pesticide-products/glyphosate
Citation 2: United States Environmental Protection Agency. (2017). Response to the final report of the FIFRA SAP on the evaluation of glyphosate. United States Environmental Protection Agency. https://cfpub.epa.gov/si/si_public_file_download.cfm?Lab=OCSPP&p_download_id=534486

Scientific Evidence: EPA incorporates updated AHS cohort analysis (Andreotti et al., 2017) showing no association between glyphosate and NHL after 17.5-year follow-up.
Legal Decision: EPA maintains non-carcinogenic classification; risk assessments finalized for public comment. EPA's conclusion becomes central defense in later litigation.
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: Over 238,000 public comments received (mostly mass mail campaigns); ~2,244 unique submissions from diverse stakeholders.
Citation 1: Reaves, E. (2020). Glyphosate Interim Registration  Review Decision Case Number 0178. US-EPA. https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/2020-01/documents/glyphosate-interim-reg-review-decision-case-num-0178.pdf

Scientific Evidence: Over 155 weed species confirmed herbicide-resistant in the US; resistance management is a widely recognized agricultural problem.
Legal Decision: Issued under FIFRA authority. Herbicide resistance elements included in every herbicide PID and ID during registration review.
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: Growers, agrichemical industry, and academic researchers collaborate on integrated pest management (IPM) frameworks. EPA finalizes Pesticide Registration Notice (PRN) on herbicide resistance management.
Citation 1: Reaves, E. (2020). Glyphosate Interim Registration  Review Decision Case Number 0178. US-EPA. https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/2020-01/documents/glyphosate-interim-reg-review-decision-case-num-0178.pdf

Scientific Evidence: Johnson's expert witnesses cited IARC classification and epidemiological studies linking glyphosate to NHL.
Legal Decision: DeWayne "Lee" Johnson v. Monsanto: firstRoundup cancer trial. Jury found Monsanto's Roundup a substantial contributing factor to Johnson's cancer, awards Johnson $289 million ($250M punitive).
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: USRTK and plaintiff attorneys file additional lawsuits; Monsanto/Bayer mobilize massive legal defense; industry allies cite EPA science.
Regulatory Outcome Categorical: Legal event — no direct regulatory change
Citation 1: U.S. Right to Know. (2018). Monsanto papers - U.S. right to know. https://usrtk.org/monsanto-papers/

Scientific Evidence: Environmental Working Group (EWG) and food company coalition petitions EPA to lower glyphosate tolerance in oats and prohibit preharvest use on oats. Court acknowledged scientific evidence but found punitive damages excessive. Scientific evidence was already sharply divided; Bayer inherited glyphosate's global liability profile.
Legal Decision: Petition filed under FFDCA; docket EPA-HQ-OPP-2019-0066 opened. Acquisition means Bayer assumes all pending and future Monsanto litigation. California 1st District Court of Appeal later upholds the grounds of the verdict but lowers damages to $20.5M. Judge William Alsup reduces Johnson's punitive damages to $39 million (total verdict ~$78 million) in the first trial. Settled via appeal; precedent set for future Roundup litigation.
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: Bayer completes its acquisition of Monsanto for $63 billion; begins setting aside >$16 billion for glyphosate litigation liability; stakeholder activism intensifies. No direct regulatory change, but Bayer becomes the primary target for all glyphosate litigation. Environmental Working Group (EWG) and food company coalition petitions EPA to lower glyphosate tolerance in oats and prohibit preharvest use on oats. Ben & Jerry's, Happy Family Organics, Nature's Path, Stonyfield Farm, and others join EWG; agricultural industry opposes restrictions.EPA acknowledges petition; response deferred until after PID.

Scientific Evidence: EPA publishes the Proposed Interim Registration Review Decision (PID) for glyphosate, maintaining it is not carcinogenic and proposing ecological mitigation. EPA withdrawls 2017 human health risk assessment
Legal Decision: EPA's PID becomes central evidence in subsequent appellate litigation.
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: EPA publishes the Proposed Interim Registration Review Decision (PID) for glyphosate, maintaining it is not carcinogenic and proposing ecological mitigation. Over 238,000 public comments submitted during the 60-day comment period; stakeholder webinars organized by EPA. California defends its Prop 65 authority; Bayer/Monsanto and industry allies press federal preemption.
Citation 1: US EPA. (2019, April 30). EPA takes next step in review process for herbicide glyphosate, reaffirms no risk to public health. Pesticides. https://www.epa.gov/pesticides/epa-takes-next-step-review-process-herbicide-glyphosate-reaffirms-no-risk-public-health

Scientific Evidence: EPA's comprehensive assessment: no risks from dietary, drinking-water, or residential exposure; ecological risks identified for non-target plants. Supporting documents include risk assessments, responses to comments, and benefits assessment.
Legal Decision: ID promulgated; interim mitigation measures imposed (spray drift, resistance management). NRDC and Rural Coalition challenge the ID in the Ninth Circuit. Third Circuit (2010) acknowledged FIFRA preemption ambiguity; subsequent cases test the scope of EPA's labeling authority. Novartis (now Syngenta) wins summary judgment in Indian Brand Farms v. Novartis on FIFRA preemption, consistent with evolving jurisprudence.
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: Environmental groups challenge the ID on health and ESA grounds; industry and farm groups support the ID. Environmental NGOs emphasize ESA risks; agricultural groups argue the ecological analysis is overstated. Wide range of stakeholders affected: farmers, environmental advocates, agricultural industry, consumer health groups. Agribusiness firms advance FIFRA preemption as a defense in all glyphosate failure-to-warn suits.
Citation 1: US EPA. (2024a, August 27). Glyphosate. EPA. Ingredients Used in Pesticide Products. https://www.epa.gov/ingredients-used-pesticide-products/glyphosate
Citation 2: US EPA, O. (2022, September 26). EPA withdraws glyphosate interim decision. Www.Epa.Gov. https://www.epa.gov/pesticides/epa-withdraws-glyphosate-interim-decision

Scientific Evidence: Ecological assessment identifies significant risks to non-target plants, which are the base of food chains for listed species.
Legal Decision: EPA initiates formal ESA consultation with US Fish & Wildlife Service and NOAA Fisheries (November 2021).
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: Consultation ongoing; partial voluntary remand sought from Ninth Circuit (May 2021). EPA issues the final Biological Evaluation for glyphosate, concluding glyphosate is "likely to adversely affect" 93% of listed species and 96% of critical habitat.
Citation 1: US EPA. (2024a, August 27). Glyphosate. EPA. Ingredients Used in Pesticide Products. https://www.epa.gov/ingredients-used-pesticide-products/glyphosate

Scientific Evidence: Court holds EPA's registration review decision is an "action" triggering ESA obligations; criticizes EPA's ecological analysis.
Legal Decision: NRDC v. EPA, 38 F.4th 34 (9th Cir. 2022). Court vacates human health ID; grants voluntary remand (without vacatur) of ecological portion.
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: Ninth Circuit vacates the human health portion of EPA's 2020 Interim Decision and imposes an October 1, 2022 deadline for a new ecological portion. Environmental groups largely vindicated; EPA unable to meet court-imposed deadline. EPA withdraws the entire Glyphosate ID in September 2022; glyphosate registrations remain but the ID is nullified.
Citation 1: US EPA, O. (2022, September 26). EPA withdraws glyphosate interim decision. Www.Epa.Gov. https://www.epa.gov/pesticides/epa-withdraws-glyphosate-interim-decision

Scientific Evidence: Settlement reflects the volume and severity of plaintiff verdicts despite scientific dispute over carcinogenicity.
Legal Decision: Mass settlement but no admission of liability; litigation continues for non-settled plaintiffs. Petition seeks to amend 40 CFR § 156.10 to codify preemption; responds to SCOTUS guidance in Bates. Consistent with Third Circuit and other rulings supporting FIFRA preemption of state health warnings. Massachusetts state court applies FIFRA preemption doctrine.
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: USRTK releases internal Monsanto documents suggesting the company knew of risks; plaintiffs' attorneys continue aggressive litigation. Bayer/Monsanto and agricultural industry groups petition EPA; environmental/health groups oppose. Defendants (Bayer/Monsanto) win a preemption victory; plaintiffs' attorneys adjust litigation strategy. Mass settlement ($10B) but no admission of liability; litigation continues for non-settled plaintiffs.

Scientific Evidence: US government argues federal pesticide labeling decisions should preempt state tort-based cancer warnings.
Legal Decision: U.S. Solicitor General recommends Supreme Court hear Monsanto's appeal in the Durnell Roundup case and sides with Monsanto on FIFRA preemption.
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: Case set for Supreme Court review; national implications for pesticide labeling law. US DOJ joins industry side; consumer/plaintiff groups file amicus opposing preemption.

Scientific Evidence: Majority opinion by Justice Kavanaugh holds that requiring a cancer warning would be "in addition to" and "different from" EPA-approved labeling.
Legal Decision: Monsanto Co. v. Durnell, 24-1068 (June 25, 2026): FIFRA expressly preempts Durnell's claim. Dissent (2 justices) argues the ruling leaves plaintiffs without remedy.
Stakeholder Interests/Actions: Agribusiness and industry hailed the ruling as bringing "containment" to litigation; consumer advocates decried the loss of accountability. Bayer states it affirms EPA's safety determination.
